narrative.overview: THOR is built like an instrument panel for engineers, not a card library for managers. The Hemeria visual language fuses the ceremonial weight of a tricolor (blue, white, red) with the live posture of a mission console. The page header is literally a 4px tricolor stripe; the sidebar is sovereign deep blue; the primary action color is a saturated console-sky that reads as 'live signal.' The work surface is an off-white tinted toward sky-blue, so even at rest the screen feels as if it sits inside a console rather than on a marketing site. The system is sharp by doctrine: every primitive ships with border-radius 0, no shadows anywhere, depth coming from tonal layering and 1px borders. Type does most of the talking: IBM Plex Sans for headings (SemiBold) and body (Regular), IBM Plex Mono for identifiers, with uppercase wide-tracked labels acting as small mission patches across cards, tabs, and table headers. Hemeria explicitly rejects the soft-SaaS aesthetic and the opposite trap of Bloomberg-Terminal black-and-amber maximalism. The palette is bright and instrumented, contrast is calm, the dominant color in any given screen is white space, and the brand red appears only as ceremony.
keyCharacteristics: Sharp corners everywhere. No border-radius on any primitive.
Flat surfaces. No shadows. Depth via 1px borders and tonal layering.
Tricolor stripe as the page-level signature.
IBM Plex Sans (SemiBold headings, Regular body) + IBM Plex Mono for identifiers.
Uppercase wide-tracked labels as mission-patch chrome.
Sky-blue is the only action color. Red is ceremonial only.

rules.name: The Sky-Is-Action Rule
rules.body: Console Sky (#006EB1) means 'do something' or 'this is selected/active.' Reserved for primary buttons, the stat-card top stripe, the sidebar active indicator, focus rings, links, and the info status. Never used as a decorative fill, gradient stop, or background tint.

rules.name: The Red-Is-Ceremony Rule
rules.body: Tricolor Red (#C80A26) appears only in the page-header stripe and the sidebar brand-lockup dot. Not the danger color. Not the destructive-action color. Engineers should not see it move or change in response to interaction.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutrals Rule
rules.body: Every gray-feeling color in the system is tinted sky-blue at very low chroma. Pure neutral gray belongs to other systems, not this one.

rules.name: The Identifier-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Every part number, document reference, affaire code, user UUID, timestamp, and tabular numeric is rendered in IBM Plex Mono with font-variant-numeric tabular-nums. Non-negotiable. Identifiers are the lingua franca of THOR; they must be visually distinguishable from prose at a glance and column-alignable in tables.

rules.name: The Heading-Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings (H1-H3, Display) are IBM Plex Sans in SemiBold (500-600) with 0.02-0.04em tracking, in Sovereign Deep Blue. Wide tracking and UPPERCASE belong to labels and eyebrows only. Body text, button labels, form inputs, table cells, error messages, toasts: Regular or Bold, never the heading weight and tracking. Using the heading style for body text breaks the system.

rules.name: The Wide-Track Caps Rule
rules.body: All uppercase text in the system uses 0.12em-0.18em letter-spacing depending on size. Uppercase without wide tracking looks shouty; with the tracking it reads as official.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No element in the Hemeria layer carries a box-shadow. If something needs to feel raised, step its surface tone (Instrument White on Cold Mist) or strengthen its border (Sovereign Deep Blue instead of Console Border). Drop shadows are forbidden, even subtle ones.

rules.name: The Reticle Rule
rules.body: The CornerFrame primitive draws four 12px corner brackets in Sovereign Deep Blue around its content. It is a heavy signature; use it sparingly, typically once per page on the most important content region. Wrapping every panel in it is wrong.

dos: Do use the PageHeader (via PreferencesHeader) as the top of every page. The tricolor stripe is the project's signature.
Do render every part number, document reference, affaire code, user ID, and timestamp in IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums.
Do use sharp corners on every primitive. border-radius: 0 is the default; do not introduce radius on new components.
Do use 1px borders and tonal layering for depth. Cold Mist beneath Instrument White beneath Hover Mist beneath Selection Veil.
Do stack toolbar / table / footrow with margin-bottom: -1px so adjacent panels share their edges into one continuous frame.
Do write button labels and pill text in IBM Plex Sans 700, 0.12em UPPERCASE.
Do keep transitions at 120ms on filter, background, and color. No transforms, no orchestration.
Do use StatusPill with semantic kind for any state indication. success / warning / danger / info are the only options.
Do use Hover Mist for interactive feedback (table-row hover, ghost-button hover, search-field background).
donts: Don't use glassmorphism. No backdrop-filter: blur, no frosted panels, no semi-transparent surfaces stacked over content.
Don't use gradients. Not on buttons, not on backgrounds, not on text, not on accent decoration. Every fill is a single solid color.
Don't introduce border-radius on any new component. The system is sharp-cornered as doctrine.
Don't add box-shadow for elevation. Use tonal layering or border weight instead.
Don't use Tricolor Red (#C80A26) for danger semantics, delete buttons, or error states. Red is ceremonial only.
Don't give body text, button text below 11px, table cells, form inputs, error messages, or toasts the heading style (SemiBold with tracking).
Don't use pure neutral gray. Every neutral in the system is tinted sky-blue at low chroma.
Don't stack StatCard four-up in a uniform metric grid (the SaaS hero-metric template).
Don't wrap Card inside Card. Nested cards are always wrong.
Don't use side-stripe colored borders on cards, callouts, alerts, or list items as decoration. The sidebar nav-active indicator is a documented functional exception.
Don't write apologetic, warm, or chatty UX copy. No 'Désolé,' no 'Oops,' no exclamation marks, no friendly suggestions.
Don't use the CornerFrame reticle on every panel. It is a heavy signature.
